summary: baserCMS administrative API authorization bypass through session fallback
details: ### Summary An authorization bypass occurs against the API endpoint `/baser/api/admin/` by abusing the session authentication fallback. ### Details The mail settings are used here as an example. Admin side: https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/master/plugins/baser-core/config/permission.php#L100 With `auth => false`, it is not accessible with operator privileges. API side: https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/master/plugins/baser-core/config/permission.php#L286 With `auth => true`, it is accessible even with operator privileges. --- First, the default group for operators has `auth_prefix = 'Admin'`, which does not include `Api/Admin`. https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/master/plugins/baser-core/src/Model/Table/UsersTable.php#L389 Because of this condition, when trying to access the `Api/Admin` API with a JWT, operators have `auth_prefix = 'Admin'`, so they cannot obtain a JWT and should not be able to access it. However, there is a problem in `getAuthenticationService`. https://github.com/baserproject/basercms/blob/master/plugins/baser-core/src/BaserCorePlugin.php#L507 Here, session authentication is enabled even for the `Api/Admin` prefix. By accessing the API with a Referer header, session authentication becomes active, allowing access to the API without holding a JWT. As a result, all APIs configured with `auth => true` in `permission.php` become accessible by operators. ### PoC 1. Log in with a site operator (operator) privileged account. 2. Run the following code in DevTools: ```javascript fetch('/baser/api/admin/baser-core/site_configs/view.json', { headers: { 'Referer': location.origin + '/baser/admin/' } }) .then(r => r.json()) .then(d => { console.table(d.siteConfig); }) ```
